subject: Final: tri-region node inventory & SOW for Atlas Labs launch
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@atlas.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary node ask for Atlas Labs Q3 launch

Irene —

Quick note from Atlas Ops: we did a traffic simulation for our Q3 feature launch and want to secure committed dedicated nodes across three regions to avoid cold-start variability. Attached is our projection workbook (high/likely/low sheets) and a short ask: 24/7 steady-state capacity to support ~120k inference requests/hour globally with peaks up to 220k.

Rough preference: A100-40GB class nodes (or equivalent); burst lanes for 30% above baseline; 95th pct latency target <150ms for text-generation path.

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood commit a tri-region allocation by July 15?
- Rough cost delta for reserved vs. on-demand routing (we’ll need pricing for committed window).
- Any regional lead-time constraints (APAC availability)?

Attaching atlas_node_request.xlsx for numbers. Happy to hop on a call next week if helpful.

—Sam
Sam Park
Head of Platform, Atlas Labs
Attachments: atlas_node_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@atlas.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary node ask for Atlas Labs Q3 launch

Sam —

Thanks for the workbook and clear targets. Looping in Ben (capacity planning) and Karthik (regional onramp) to size this against our current node inventory and procurement timeline. Quick clarifying items so we can produce a firm commit and SOW:

- Confirm the inference profile: are those 120k/220k requests/hour counting short chat sessions (avg 35 tokens) or long-form completions (avg 220 tokens)?
- Is the 95th <150ms target for cold-starts included or only steady-state? We can usually guarantee steady-state but cold-start P95 will be higher unless you accept prefix caching.
- Any data residency or KMS constraints per region? (procurement will ask).

We will draft a SOW with node counts per region and a tentative timeline. Ben/Karthik — can you put a preliminary node split + earliest activation dates on this thread?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary node ask for Atlas Labs Q3 launch — initial sizing

Irene / team —

Ran their high/likely/low through our capacity model. Assumptions I used (call these out so sales can validate with Atlas): avg request = 60 tokens, model variant = 7B quantized (sustains higher throughput), sustained concurrency target = 480 qps global at baseline, burst factor 1.3.

Initial proposed committed pool (A100-40GB equiv):
- US (east/us-central): 8 nodes (baseline) + 2 burst lanes
- EU (frankfurt/ams): 5 nodes + 1 burst lane
- APAC (singapore): 4 nodes + 1 burst lane

Notes / tradeoffs:
- If Atlas can accept higher quantization (4-bit tuned) we can reduce physical node count by ~25% with minor latency tradeoffs.
- APAC lead time: procurement & certs make Singapore nodes ~6–8 weeks to activate; we can offer temporary routing to US-edge with degraded P95 (~40–60ms uplift).
- Autoscale policy: start with steady reserved baseline and allow 2x burst autoscale for short windows.

Attachments: calculation_summary.csv (I can upload if useful)

Laura — can you confirm procurement/contract lead time and whether we can accelerate via a marketplace listing?

—Ben
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preliminary node ask for Atlas Labs Q3 launch — APAC nuance

Ben / Irene —

Agree with Ben's split but flagging two operational constraints for APAC:
1) Singapore region quota is currently constrained for A100-40GB; lead time is 6–10 weeks for new rack allocation unless we use partner colocations (adds networking setup).
2) KMS key provisioning + compliance scan for Atlas (they mentioned residency) will add ~1 week if they already have a validated KMS flow; otherwise plan for 2–3 weeks.

Practical mitigation: start with a phased APAC plan — provision 2 nodes in APAC within 6 weeks for canary traffic (10–15% of baseline), route remainder via US-edge for the first 6 weeks. We'll run a 2-week canary and capture observed P95 uplift and token-cost delta. If Atlas signs SOW this week we can reserve the inventory window and meet an APAC full ramp by ~10 weeks.

Quoted from Ben earlier:
> APAC lead time: procurement & certs make Singapore nodes ~6–8 weeks to activate; we can offer temporary routing to US-edge with degraded P95 (~40–60ms uplift).

Karthik
Head of Field Ops — APAC, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@atlas.ai>, Atlas Labs Procurement <procurement@atlas.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 May 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Action: confirm SOW & tri-region node commit for Atlas Labs (next steps)

Sam —

Thanks for the clear requirements. Summary and proposed commitments below (we will convert to an SOW and send via DocuSign once you confirm):

1) Commit (A100-40GB equiv) — reserved baseline + burst lanes
   - US: 8 baseline + 2 burst (activate target: 6 weeks after SOW signature)
   - EU: 5 baseline + 1 burst (activate target: 8 weeks after SOW signature)
   - APAC: 2 baseline (canary) + 1 burst initially; full APAC ramp to 4 baseline + 1 burst by ~10 weeks post-signature.

2) Performance SLOs
   - Steady-state 95th percentile latency target: <150ms (Redwood will rely on prefix caching to meet cold-starts where agreed).
   - Canary window: 2 weeks of progressively increasing traffic in APAC; we will supply latency dashboards and unit-cost delta.

3) Pricing & commitments
   - We will provide a 12-month committed price in the SOW with optional tranches; follow-up email will include a committed vs. on-demand delta table.

4) Next steps
   - Atlas: confirm acceptance of the node split and sign the attached SOW draft (sow-draft-AtlasLabs-v1.pdf) or request edits by EOD Tue, 31 May.
   - Redwood: once SOW signed we will reserve inventory and schedule activation dates per region.

Attachments: sow-draft-AtlasLabs-v1.pdf (SOW draft), atlas_node_request.xlsx (customer projection)
Related links: https://crm.redwood.example/h/ATL-2027-Q3-42 (HubSpot record), DocuSign send: https://docusign.example/s/ABC123

CC-ing Laura and Vivek for procurement and executive visibility. Laura — can procurement confirm whether a Marketplace expedite is possible to shave 1–2 weeks? Vivek — flagging for revenue ops FYI.

Happy to take a short call tomorrow if that helps finalize.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
